title: Energy Transfer in Ecosystems
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Energy Transfer in Ecosystems Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Energy flows through ecosystems from producers to consumers along food chains and food webs; only about 10% of the energy passes to the next trophic level; ecological pyramids show energy, numbers and biomass. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 7, Quarter 2: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Life Science): food chains and webs, trophic levels, the 10% rule, ecological pyramids and decomposers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: About 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.
body_html:
How to think about it

Producers (plants and algae) capture energy from sunlight by photosynthesis. Herbivores are primary consumers; carnivores are secondary and tertiary consumers; decomposers break down dead matter. Each feeding level is a trophic level.

At each level most energy is used for life processes or lost as heat, so only about 10% passes on. This is why food chains are short and top predators are few. Ecological pyramids of energy, numbers and biomass show this pattern.

Example

Producers have 10,000 kJ. About how much reaches primary consumers?

10%

Answer: 1,000 kJ

Example

Which organisms return nutrients to the soil?

Bacteria and fungi

Answer: decomposers

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled in an ecosystem.
  • Drawing food chain arrows the wrong way (arrows show where energy goes).
  • Leaving decomposers out of a food web.

faq.q: Why are there more rice plants than rice birds in a field?
faq.a: Energy decreases at each level, so higher levels support fewer organisms.

faq.q: Why do arrows point from the plant to the animal?
faq.a: They show the direction energy flows.

items.q: The producers contain 15,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and the primary consumers contain 1,200 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer.
